answer: A practical sybil defense is to tie every agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to free account creation. Each vertex in the trust graph earns weight only after completing checkable tasks, paying a small cost, and being vouched for by already-established peers. Like quartz forming under pressure over time, reputation should accumulate slowly and be hard to fake in bulk. A newcomer therefore faces a long horizon before it can influence rewards, while a sudden swarm of fresh identities stays at the edge, visible and low-weight, instead of flooding the core.
